real_estate.homebuilder: Bay Area home prices kept pace with inflation while the nation's slipped for a 16th month.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates fell. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.26%, down 0.06 from Tuesday and 0.20 from a week ago, with the 15-year at 6.82%. On today's $1,218,320 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $6,655 a month in principal and interest.

Home prices are rising, just not faster than everything else. S&P's Case-Shiller national index rose 2.1% in the year to September while consumer prices rose 3.7%, the 16th straight month home prices fell after inflation, S&P said Tuesday. Market Briefs had those numbers right.

The Bay Area did better (chart). The San Francisco metro index, which covers Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, San Francisco and San Mateo counties, rose 3.73%, fifth of 19 metros and even with inflation to the rounding. Only Chicago, New York, Miami and Cleveland beat inflation.

Wednesday's export shows 2,157 board wide, from 2,207 Tuesday, with 139 coming soon and 66 brand new. The five city ledger is 555, from 562: Fremont (196) added one, Hayward (156) lost six, Milpitas (82) lost two, and Newark (67) and Union City (54) held.

What this means for you: if you own here, your home has about held its value after inflation over the past year, which most of the country cannot say. If you are buying, the holiday weeks bring fewer competing buyers, and 191 homes in our five cities have been on the market 60 days or longer.

• Board wide: 2,157 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 139 coming soon and 66 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 555 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 482 are on the market and 73 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 196 live, 157 active, 28 coming soon and 9 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,218,320 at $783 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 41 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 156, Milpitas 82, Newark 67, Union City 54.
• Across all five cities the median is $999,894 at $667 a square foot. 244 homes are priced under a million, and 191 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

U.S. national 2.1%.

stocks.news:
Nvidia slid for a second day. It fell 3.91% to $149.30, leaving it 19.9% below where it started the year, and Micron lost 4.53%. The Nasdaq fell 0.62% and the S&P 500 0.25%, while the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Anthropic rose 1.08% to $82.79, still below its $83 offering price.

Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday's session ends early, at 10 a.m. Pacific. Chip investors could use the long weekend.

economy.note: The 10-Year is Treasury's official Wednesday close. Gold and silver are Wednesday's December COMEX settlements. Brent is Tuesday's ICE settlement (January), the latest from our locked source.
economy.commentary:
Consumers are in a better mood. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, back to levels last seen in January 2025, as 30.8% of consumers said jobs are plentiful, up from 26.2% in October. Plans to buy homes improved slightly, though consumers still expect 5.7% inflation over the next year.

China kept its ban on U.S.-bound gallium, germanium and antimony on hold through Jan. 27, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, extending a pause that was due to end Friday. The U.S. Geological Survey puts China's share of 2025 world production at 99% for low purity gallium, used in chips, 80% for natural graphite, used in batteries, and 36% for mined antimony, where Russia and Tajikistan together mine nearly half (chart).

The 10-year Treasury closed at 4.85%, down 0.06 point. Gold settled at $3,535.80, down 0.73%, and silver at $40.06, down 1.78%. Brent settled Tuesday at $91.40, up 2.27%.

Shoppers are feeling better just in time for Black Friday. Their credit cards get the final say.
